transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery. But after that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening.

Just remember to avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that helps! Next, I'm curious about when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be fine to keep using it as you were before. If you're unsure about anything specific, your GP can also help.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that's good to know. I'm also experiencing some sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let us know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, some sensitivity to light is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity - especially if your eye is also red and painful - that's not normal and we may need to assess it further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that clarifies things for me. I had my surgery about a week ago, so it seems to be just as you described. I appreciate your help, and I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! So just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!
